title: $D^b_{ctf}=D^b_c$ for integral and rational coefficients
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside it, with valuation ring $\cO_E$. Use the condensed coefficient rings of [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed], pulled back to the small pro-étale site. Let $X$ be a qcqs scheme and $\Lambda\in\{\mathbf Z_\ell,\cO_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Qlb\}$. Then:

1. every constructible $\Lambda_X$-module has Tor amplitude in $[-1,0]$, and in $[0,0]$ if
   $\Lambda$ is a field;
2. every $K\in\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ with cohomology in $[a,b]$ has Tor amplitude in $[a-1,b]$;
   hence $\Dctf(X,\Lambda)=\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and
   $\Loc(\Dctf(X,\Lambda))=\Loc(\Dbc(X,\Lambda))$.

The following counterexamples are over the scalar ring, or as constant sheaves on $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$ for a separably closed field $k$. For scalar complexes, perfect means isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated projective modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]; for the constant-sheaf examples, perfect means locally isomorphic to such a complex of finite projective $A_X$-modules. For a finite nonregular ring the condition is essential: $\mathbf F_\ell$ over
$\mathbf Z/\ell^2$ is constructible but has infinite projective dimension. Finite Tor
amplitude is a condition on the whole complex: for $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^2$ the complex
$[A\xrightarrow{\ell}A]$ is perfect, whereas its nonzero cohomology modules are
$\mathbf F_\ell$, which are not perfect. So for every qcqs scheme $X$ and every finite commutative ring $A$
(with its discrete condensed structure), $\Dctf(X,A)$ is thick, but it need not be stable
under standard truncations (already for $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^2$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}k$).

proof.text: Apply the uniform finite-constant-local-model interval theorem, with c=-1 for the integral DVR coefficients and c=0 for field coefficients. Enlarge the field interval to [-1,0]. Rearrange the coefficient disjunction into the six-case convention of the stratified devissage theorem; its finite-ring alternative is not needed here.

Apply finite-strata Tor devissage to the local-model bound on every scheme. This gives [-1,0] for every constructible module and, when the coefficient is a field, [0,0]. The main theorem uses the stated devissage declaration rather than reproving its open-closed induction.

Apply the cohomology-interval theorem with [c,d]=[-1,0] to get [a-1,b]. Boundedness supplies endpoints; replacing the lower one by min(a,b) ensures an ordered interval even for zero complexes. Thus every bounded constructible object has finite Tor amplitude. Extensionality identifies Dbc intersect finiteTor with Dbc, and congruence gives equality of their localizing closures.

For finite discrete A, use the normalized exact fixed-module encoding and its constructibility comparison. Smallify each pro-etale covering family; this identifies ordinary local models with finite locally constant fixed modules and their stratifications. Constructible fixed modules form a Serre class by the finite-ring kernel/cokernel and extension theorems. Apply cohomology in a weak Serre class and boundedness for triangulation. A retract is ker(1-r i); applying homology preserves retracts and vanishing intervals, giving bounded constructible retract closure. Pull these properties back through the exact derived encoding and intersect with the already thick finite-Tor property.

For Z/ell^2, prove directly that ell squared is zero and its annihilator is (ell). The periodic tensor theorem gives F=A/(ell) in every nonpositive degree of the derived self-tensor. F is nontrivial, so it has no finite Tor bound; a finite projective resolution would force high Tor to vanish, proving infinite projective dimension. The cone of ell on A[0] is a two-term finite projective complex, hence perfect. A perfect complex has a bounded flat model, so F[0] cannot be perfect. These scalar conclusions are proved in the parent module without additional holes.

Apply the constant square-zero example theorem at each separably closed Spec k. Its displayed quotient is definitionally the constantResidueModuleOnSpec used in the parent. The theorem supplies constructibility and infinite Tor amplitude for this module, and a bounded constructible finite-Tor complex whose upper truncation has infinite Tor amplitude. Forgetting the truncation constructibility conjunct yields exactly the claimed failure.
